text:
Most visitors eat their Sapporo seafood bowl at Nijo Market downtown. The market next to the city's wholesale market is about 20 minutes from Odori, has around 60 shops and 20 or so restaurants, and fills with local workers at lunch 👇

🎯 Bet you can't guess what's hidden inside that market (it isn't food) 👉 https://japanbystation.com/sapporo-where-locals-eat

We put this together from Sapporo's official tourism pages and checked every opening time.

🦀 BREAKFAST: CURB MARKET

Tozai Line from Odori to Nijuyonken, about 10 minutes, then a 7-minute walk. It's open 6:00 to 17:00 (restaurants from 7:00), every day. Most fish shops have a dining room, so you eat what you just picked. Go between 8:00 and 11:00, when the stock is best.

🐟 SHORT ON TIME: NIJO MARKET

Downtown by Bus Center-mae, with shops over 100 years old. Restaurants open 6:00 to 21:00, so it also works for an early dinner.

🍛 SOUP CURRY

Garaku, in a basement near Odori, simmers its broth for two days and closes when it runs out. Or ride out to Kotoni, where Picante cooks each curry in its own small pot under the JR station.

🍜 RAMEN

The famous alley in Susukino has 17 miso ramen shops, and it's where locals end a night out. Keyaki, around the corner, serves until 2 a.m. every day.

👉 The free breakfast shuttle most visitors never hear about, plus the full eating route:
https://japanbystation.com/sapporo-where-locals-eat

Seafood bowl, soup curry or miso ramen: which comes first for you?
